name: What is the difference between pool fill-in and pool demolition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between pool fill-in, pool demolition, and pool removal?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between pool fill-in, pool demolition, and pool removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: These terms are often used loosely, but they do not always mean the same thing. Pool fill-in usually refers to a project where the pool is drained, openings are made for drainage, part of the structure may be removed, and the cavity is backfilled and compacted. Pool demolition refers to breaking down the pool structure, which may be partial or complete. Pool removal can mean leaving some of the shell in place and filling over it, or it can mean full excavation and hauling away all debris. The main difference is how much of the shell is removed and what the site is intended to support afterward. A partial removal is typically less expensive, while a full removal may be preferred if the area will support future construction, major hardscape, or a load-bearing landscape design. Homeowners should ask the contractor to define the scope in writing so there is no confusion about drainage, compaction, export, and final grading.
acceptedAnswer.description: Pool fill-in usually means draining the pool, breaking up or removing part of the shell for drainage, and backfilling the cavity. Pool demolition and pool removal can mean either partial removal with backfill or complete excavation and export of the shell. The right option depends on budget, future land use, and local permit rules.
